answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post bids or earn reputation. The protocol rate-limits new bonded accounts and lets peers challenge suspicious clusters; if a challenge proves that supposedly independent agents share one controller, their bonds are forfeited and rewards redistributed. A whisper from a haven or an ivory-tower operator earns no special trust: the attacker must fund each identity, keep capital locked, and risk losing it, making large-scale sybil farming expensive rather than free.
